nodes.name: Carbon paper cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of CP (4 cm × 3 cm × 0.19 mm) was cleaned by ultrasonication in acetone for 15 min, and then dried in air.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal WO3/CP synthesis
nodes.procedure: (NH4)6H2W12O40·xH2O (4.0 mmol, 11.825 g) was dissolved in 60.0 ml ultrapure water, followed by magnetic stirring for 20 min to obtain a homogeneous solution. The above solution was transferred into a 100 ml autoclave and CP was placed vertically in the solution. Then, the autoclave was heated at 180°C for 16 h. The obtained WO3/CP was washed in deionized water and dried at 70°C overnight.

nodes.name: WO3-x/CP reduction
nodes.procedure: WO3/CP (1 cm × 1.5 cm) was annealed at 400°C for 2 h at a heating rate of 5°C/min in H2/Ar (10/90) atmosphere to obtain WO3-x/CP.

nodes.name: RuCl3 impregnation
nodes.procedure: RuCl3 (40.0 mg) was dissolved in 20.0 ml deionized water by magnetic stirring and ultrasonication to obtain 2.0 mg/ml RuCl3 solution. WO3/CP (1 cm × 1.5 cm) was immersed in 10 ml 2.0 mg/ml RuCl3 solution for 2 min. Subsequently, the WO3/CP was taken out and dried in an infrared desiccator for 8 min to obtain RuCl3·WO3/CP.

nodes.name: Ru-WO3/CP chemical reduction
nodes.procedure: NaBH4 (100.0 mg) was dissolved in 20.0 ml 1.0 M NaOH solution under magnetic stirring to obtain 5.0 mg/ml NaBH4 solution. WO3/CP (1 cm × 1.5 cm) was immersed in 10 ml 2.0 mg/ml RuCl3 solution for 2 min. Subsequently, the WO3/CP was taken out and dried in an infrared desiccator for 8 min to obtain RuCl3·WO3/CP. Finally, RuCl3·WO3/CP was immersed in 5.0 mg/ml NaBH4 solution for 10 min to obtain Ru-WO3/CP.

nodes.description: HER performance of commercial Ru/C (5.0 wt%) in 1.0 M PBS
nodes.source_text: The HER activity of commercial Ru/C (5.0 wt.%) electrocatalyst was first evaluated in 1.0 M PBS (Fig. 1a). The Ru/C electrocatalyst displays a large overpotential of 86 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm-2 with a Tafel slope as large as 78 mV dec-1.

nodes.description: HER performance comparison in 1.0 M PBS (includes WO3-x/CP baseline)
nodes.source_text: The HER performance of the as-prepared electrocatalysts was examined in a three-electrode system in N2 saturated 1.0 M PBS. In comparison to WO3-x/CP and commercial Ru/C (5.0 wt.%)/CP, the Ru-WO3-x/CP exhibits a greatly improved HER activity, reaching a current density of 10 mA cm-2 at an overpotential as low as 19 mV... enhanced by a factor of 24.0... Tafel slope... significantly reduces to 41 mV dec-1... low overpotential of 225 mV to achieve a current density of 1 A cm-2

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-WO3-x/CP displays clear diffraction peaks of hexagonal WO3 (JCPDS No. 85-2460) with peaks shifted to high angles indicating lattice shrinkage due to oxygen vacancies; no Ru peaks detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of the as-prepared Ru-WO3-x/CP catalyst was examined by X-ray diffraction (XRD) as shown in Fig. 2b. The Ru · WO3-x/CP displays clear diffraction peaks of hexagonal WO3 (JCPDS No. 85-2460), but no diffraction peaks related to Ru NPs...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of hexagonal WO3 and hexagonal Ru; WO3 lattice fringes at edge become blurred due to oxygen vacancies; average Ru NP size is 3.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both lattice spacings resulting from hexagonal WO3 and hexagonal Ru are clearly visible in the HRTEM images of Ru-WO3-x/CP (Fig. 2c, d... the average size of the Ru NPs on Ru-WO3-x/CP is 3.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mappings reveal uniform distribution of Ru, W, and O elements in Ru-WO3-x/CP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX elemental mappings reveal uniform distribution of Ru, W and O elements (Supplementary Fig. 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru mass content in Ru-WO3-x/CP determined to be 5.1 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass content of Ru in Ru · WO3-x/CP was determined to be 5.1 wt.% by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) (Supplementary Table 7).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR confirms formation of oxygen vacancies in Ru-WO3-x/CP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of oxygen vacancies in Ru-WO3-x/CP was confirmed by the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurement as shown in Fig. 2e.
